assessmentSummary.identity: A hands-and-knees or declared heel-sit quadruped action in which one palm-up arm reaches beneath the torso, reverses, and rotates open while the support shoulder and pelvis remain controlled.
currentCardFindings: Quadruped Thread-the-Needle, Reach, and Rotation name the same reach-under then open action.
Standard and heel-sit support are exact selectable variants; range and pause are modifiers.
Four links have healthy oEmbed metadata only and remain unviewed candidate media.

currentCardSnapshot.description: From an exact hands-and-knees or declared heel-sit quadruped base, keep the support arm active and pelvis controlled, reach the moving arm palm-up beneath the torso through pain-free range, then reverse and rotate it open as the eyes follow the hand. Exhale through the owned range, return without momentum, and stop before shoulder support, pelvic control, breathing, or symptom-free motion changes.

population.medicalScope: The card does not diagnose, treat, or clear symptoms; follow the athlete care plan and local scope.

claims: Privacy-enhanced YouTube embed URLs can be constructed with youtube-nocookie.com.

The candidate watch URLs returned oEmbed metadata on 2026-07-26; embed playback, full-video exact matching, cue and safety quality, captions, accessibility, reviewer identity, and approval remain unresolved.

evidence.sourceTitle: Thoracic Mobility Exercises to Address Shoulder Pain
claims: The defining action is a quadruped reach under the torso followed by a controlled reversal into open rotation.
The added words reach or rotation name existing phases and do not create separate exercise identities.

evidence.sourceTitle: Thoracic Mobility Exercises to Address Shoulder Pain
claims: Declare the support base, moving side, palm-up thread, open rotation, owned range, tempo, repetitions, and pelvic-control standard.
Side-lying rotation and hand-behind-head rotation without a thread-under path remain separate definitions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Clinical reasoning framework for thoracic spine exercise prescription in sport: a systematic review and narrative synthesis
claims: Thoracic rotation coordinates spinal, rib-cage, scapular, shoulder, and trunk musculature while one arm provides closed-chain support.
The card does not claim muscle isolation or exact activation magnitude.

evidence.sourceTitle: Clinical reasoning framework for thoracic spine exercise prescription in sport: a systematic review and narrative synthesis
claims: Quadruped thoracic rotation appears in the exercise literature, and heel-sit positioning can constrain lumbar and pelvic contribution.
Exact pain-free range and contact comfort remain individual selection constraints.

evidence.sourceTitle: Clinical reasoning framework for thoracic spine exercise prescription in sport: a systematic review and narrative synthesis
claims: Complexity rises with a heel-sit constraint, greater owned range, longer pauses, and stricter pelvic control.
Exercise difficulty uses complexity and physical demand only, with overall equal to their maximum.

evidence.sourceTitle: Clinical reasoning framework for thoracic spine exercise prescription in sport: a systematic review and narrative synthesis
claims: Loading is bodyweight support through one hand and both knees while the other arm moves.
Track support-shoulder, wrist, and trunk fatigue plus loss of support, range, pelvic control, or breath.

evidence.sourceTitle: Thoracic Mobility Exercises to Address Shoulder Pain
claims: Use a stable nonslip surface, comfortable wrist and knee contacts, clear reach space, and a safe floor transfer.
Do not use through pain, neurologic symptoms, dizziness, or unsafe support.

evidence.sourceTitle: Thoracic Mobility Exercises to Address Shoulder Pain
claims: Use slow side-balanced quality repetitions and controlled breathing rather than fatigue-seeking volume.
Stop before range shrinks, compensation rises, support collapses, or symptoms appear.

evidence.sourceTitle: Thoracic Mobility Exercises to Address Shoulder Pain
claims: Set the base, declare the side, thread palm-up, reverse without momentum, open through owned range, and return.
Instruction includes breathing, range, dose, quality gate, stop rules, and finish.

evidence.sourceTitle: Thoracic Mobility Exercises to Address Shoulder Pain
claims: Stop for symptoms, support collapse, pelvic spin, forced range, breath holding, or unsafe floor conditions.
A symptom-free shorter range is preferred to forcing an endpoint.

evidence.sourceTitle: Clinical reasoning framework for thoracic spine exercise prescription in sport: a systematic review and narrative synthesis
claims: Use only when the drill improves or preserves rotation quality for the intended session context.
Direct outcome evidence for the exact exercise and variants is limited, so universal transfer is not claimed.

evidence.sourceTitle: Thoracic Mobility Exercises to Address Shoulder Pain
claims: Athlete guidance names expected and unexpected sensations, self-checks, accessibility choices, and nonvideo instruction.
The athlete reports symptoms and side differences rather than forcing symmetry.

evidence.sourceTitle: Clinical reasoning framework for thoracic spine exercise prescription in sport: a systematic review and narrative synthesis
claims: The coach observes support, pelvis, thorax, breath, range, reversal, and side symmetry.
Record the exact variant, side, range, dose, compensation, symptoms, and stop reason.

evidence.sourceTitle: Thoracic Mobility Exercises to Address Shoulder Pain
claims: Padding, shorter range, fewer repetitions, slower motion, standard quadruped, and side-lying substitution can improve access.
A different support configuration requires exact variant review.

evidence.sourceTitle: Clinical reasoning framework for thoracic spine exercise prescription in sport: a systematic review and narrative synthesis
claims: Heel-sit support is a variant and shorter range is a modifier.
Side-lying Open Book, hand-behind-head rotation, loaded work, and ballistic work require separate definitions.
